title: automat control artifact
description: A compiled, frozen control set. automat interprets this document at vend time; it never interprets raw upstream catalog formats. Deliberately a strict subset of OSCAL component-definition concepts so upstream suites can adopt it.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this schema. Consumers must reject major versions they do not know.

sources.description: Provenance of the compile. Every input that influenced controls[] must appear here with a hash.

compiled_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp, second precision, 'Z' suffix.

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the canonicalized CONTENT PAYLOAD: the object {controls, region_deny_exempt_services}, not the controls[] array alone. Both members are semantic — region_deny_exempt_services names the service namespaces a region or service Deny must spare, so an edit adding one widens a hole in that Deny — and a hash covering only controls[] would leave that field unhashed and every signature over the artifact silent about it. Excluded from the payload: schema_version, and the artifact block itself (which carries this value, and whose sources entries are each vouched for by their own sha256). internal/artifact enumerates the covered and excluded field names so that adding a field to the artifact fails the build until its hash coverage is decided.

region_deny_exempt_services.description:
The service namespaces a REGION Deny must not cover, as DATA rather than a list compiled into the tool.

Globally addressed services are reached through endpoints AWS reports as us-east-1, so a Deny on every action outside a region allowlist denies every IAM call, every STS call, and every Organizations call in the account — including the operator's own ability to undo it. Getting this list wrong bricks an account, which is precisely the argument for it being reviewable catalog content: the same argument `exempt_principals` rests on. A list only the binary knows is a control whose scope cannot be reviewed, and cannot be corrected without a release.

ARTIFACT-LEVEL rather than per control, and not for tidiness. Its scope IS the artifact: two controls in one document carrying different lists would have no coherent meaning, and a control-level field also made this an `scp` block on a control that denies nothing, which a `baseline-protection` control is not allowed to be. An AWS fact about which endpoints answer where is not a Deny and must not be shaped like one.

INTERSECTED under union, and that is forced rather than chosen. A `Deny` over `NotAction: [a:*]` concatenated with a `Deny` over `NotAction: [b:*]` denies everything except the INTERSECTION, so a merge that unioned these lists would describe something the rendered policy does not do. The consequence is that the list only ever shrinks as control sets merge, and an intersection reaching empty is a hard error at plan time rather than an attached deny-all.

Deliberately NOT required alongside `region_allowlist`: the control set stating an AWS fact need not be the one restricting regions — automat's own `baseline-protection` supplies this list and constrains no regions. The pairing is a PLAN-TIME invariant instead. If any compiled input constrains regions and none supplies this list, the packer refuses to render rather than falling back to a built-in, because a fallback is the compiled-in list with extra steps.

artifact_id.description: Stable, lowercase, filesystem- and tag-safe identifier.

source.description: One compile input. Exactly one of catalog/mapping/artifact names the kind of input.

mapping.description: Enforcement mapping source, e.g. an AWS Config conformance pack.

artifact.description: An input control artifact, when this artifact is a union (DESIGN 9).

note.description: Provenance caveat. Required by ROADMAP Phase 0 where a mapping is partial or absent.

id.description: Canonical control identifier in its authoritative numbering.

crosswalk.description: Equivalent identifiers in other frameworks. This is what lets union dedupe one practice across frameworks (DESIGN 9).

enforcement.description: How automat enforces or monitors this control. A control may carry several classes.

enforcement_class.description: scp: preventive, enforced by a service control policy. config-rule: detective, monitored by AWS Config. procedural: requires documented human process; produces an attestation stub. baseline-protection: an SCP that guards automat's own baseline (DESIGN 10).

scp.description: Service control policy fragment(s). Deny-style strongly preferred: deny statements concatenate safely under union (DESIGN 9).

region_allowlist.description: Permitted regions. Intersected under union, never widened.

service_allowlist.description: Permitted service namespaces. Intersected under union, never widened.

effect.description: Deny only. An Allow in an SCP merely widens what a parent SCP already permits, so it does not compose under union: the union of control sets must be an intersection of permitted behavior (DESIGN 9). Region and service allowlists are the supported way to express permission, and are intersected rather than concatenated.

condition.description: IAM condition block: operator -> condition key -> value(s).

exempt_principals.description: Principals the SCP packer must exempt from this Deny, each with a reason. An exemption is the one thing in a catalog that WIDENS a policy, so the list is capped, every entry must justify itself, and under union these lists are INTERSECTED, never concatenated (DESIGN 9): an exemption present in only one input control set is not carried into the merged artifact.

exempt_principal.description: One hole in a Deny, and the reason it exists.

reason.description: Why this principal must be exempt. Required because an unexplained exemption is indistinguishable from one added to create an escape hatch, and the reviewer of a baseline-protection catalog is reading for exactly that.

exempt_principal_ref.description: Either the symbolic token for automat's own in-account automation role, whose ARN is not known until vend time and which the packer materializes, or a literal IAM role ARN a catalog author supplies. Only these two forms: the ARN pattern admits no wildcard and no principal type other than role, so neither a whole account nor the root user can be exempted — which is what keeps the root-user Deny in DESIGN 10 from being undone by an exemption entry.

config_rule.description: One AWS Config managed rule bound to a control, with the provenance of that binding.

identifier.description: AWS Config managed rule source identifier, e.g. IAM_PASSWORD_POLICY.

name.description: Config rule name as deployed, e.g. iam-password-policy.

rationale.description: Why this rule is bound to this control. Required for curated bindings, where no upstream mapping vouches for the association.

binding_provenance.description: Who asserts that this rule enforces this control. aws-mapping: the binding comes from a published AWS mapping recorded in artifact.sources, and is mechanically generated — never hand-edited. curated: the binding is this project's own judgment, and must carry a rationale.

config_rule_parameter.description: A rule parameter plus the partial order used to resolve conflicts under union (DESIGN 9).

value.description: The parameter value. For set-union and set-intersect orders this is a separator-joined set; see set_separator.

set_separator.description: Separator splitting value into set members, for set-union and set-intersect orders. Defaults to "," when absent.

allOf.comment: A set-valued parameter must carry at least one member. An empty set is not a stricter set: AWS Config rejects it, and under set-intersect it absorbs every set it is resolved against. With the default separator this is checkable directly; a value made entirely of a non-default separator is caught by the Go validator, which is authoritative on member splitting.

parameter_order.description: How union resolves two control sets binding the same parameter (DESIGN 9). Every order must be monotone: the resolved value never permits behavior either input forbade. min: the smaller value is stricter. max: the larger value is stricter. exact: no ordering; conflicting values are a hard error requiring an explicit override. set-union: the value is a set of prohibited items, so the union of both sets is stricter. set-intersect: the value is a set of permitted items, so the intersection of both sets is stricter.

template.description: Template filename relative to the artifact's attestation template set.
